PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called meeting to order at 5:16 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on Closed Session agenda items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:18 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:12 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:  Items #1 and #2 - staff provided a presentation, the City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on these items.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the regular meeting to order at 6:13 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Transportation Director McFerguson led the Pledge of Allegiance

INVOCATION Mayor Argumedo offered the invocation.  

5.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce  -  Action: receive and filed (Pass) Moved by Mireya Garcia 
Sergeant Duarte presented an overview of the 2023 statistics, comparing them with those of 2022 to identify changes and areas for improvement. Councilmember Garcia requested a breakdown of residential and business robberies, while Councilmember Rebollo asked for a separation of crime statistics between Commerce Shopping Center and Citadel.

Mayor Argumedo expressed gratitude to Sergeant Duarte for organizing Coffee with the Deputies and for actively engaging the community through Neighborhood Watch meetings. The Mayor also appreciated Public Safety Manager Edson for his responsiveness to residents' concerns and immediate actions on some issues. Mayor Argumedo highlighted the importance of security cameras and encouraged community members, especially newcomers, to participate in the security camera program. The Mayor emphasized the need to promote the program and motivate residents to install security systems.

In response to Councilmember Rebollo's request, Sergeant Duarte mentioned exploring evening times for Coffee with the Deputies and considering different ideas.

PUBLIC COMMENT Scott Mainzen, the General Manager of Syserco Energy Solutions Inc., expressed confidence in his company's ability to excel in the project. He highlighted that Syserco employs fully union labor. Mr. Mainzen recommended that the City Council prioritize the best interests of their constituents, and encouraging consideration of Syserco for the project.

7.. Committee and Commission Appointments Mayor Argumedo appointed Jesus Dimas to the Planning Commission.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS The Councilmembers and Mayor extended their congratulations to the Commerce Dance Team for their victory in a Hawaii tournament, as well as to the Crush Volleyball, Water Polo, and Aces teams for their recent accomplishments.

Mayor Argumedo emphasized the need to begin new projects in the upcoming year that will elevate the city's status as a top destination. He highlighted the importance of advancing specific projects that bring positive developments to the city.

ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 6:42 p.m. in memory of Raul Elenes Jr.
